domain_reasoning: Writing step-by-step procedure text to documentation standards is mostly reading and writing a document.
length_reasoning: A simple procedure for a small feature takes under half an hour; a long multi-environment or regulated procedure takes a couple of hours.
review_reasoning: The reviewer opens the document and checks it is clear and follows the template; a typical one needs steps compared with the actual test run.
stakes_reasoning: A vague step is found when someone else repeats the test, but in regulated settings a non-compliant procedure can fail an audit.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's templates, standards and product knowledge, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into entering the refund, exchange or adjustment in the billing or order system.
length_reasoning: A simple refund is a couple of minutes of entry and confirmation; an adjustment needing several line items or look-ups takes over ten.
review_reasoning: A reviewer listens to the entry and confirmation part of the call and checks the system record.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong amount reaches the customer and needs a correction, usually caught soon; a large or repeated error is a financial loss.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's systems and refund rules, picked up over a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is writing the problem, steps and outcome as notes; operating the ticket tool is minor.
length_reasoning: A routine problem takes a few minutes to write up; a multi-step investigation takes a quarter of an hour.
review_reasoning: The lead reads the notes and checks they are complete and match the outcome; no need to repeat the work.
stakes_reasoning: Poor notes cost time to whoever picks up the ticket later but rarely cause direct harm.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's ticket conventions and the local systems named in the notes, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Most of the time goes into operating the billing or order system to enter the remedy and noting the case.
length_reasoning: A simple refund from a queued case takes a few minutes; an adjustment needing records checked or several systems takes half an hour.
review_reasoning: The supervisor or finance opens the case and compares the entry with the approved remedy and amount.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong amount or account causes a customer complaint and a correction, and a large one is a financial loss.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's billing systems, approval limits and policies, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into reviewing the case file and system before and during the call.
length_reasoning: A simple result call takes a few minutes; explaining a claim outcome or adjustment with many questions takes a quarter of an hour.
review_reasoning: A QA reviewer listens to the recorded call, partly at higher speed, and checks accuracy against the case.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong or unclear explanation to the customer causes complaints and follow-up calls but can be corrected, though a wrong claim statement may carry legal exposure.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's claim and adjustment rules and case system, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Writing a standard or criteria document is mostly reading and writing, with discussion and review of past releases.
length_reasoning: A simple checklist or short criteria set takes a few hours of active work; a full standard needing data and stakeholder input takes days.
review_reasoning: The manager reads the document and judges whether it is sound and workable, which needs context and some checking against practice.
stakes_reasoning: Poor criteria cause bad release decisions, which show up only later, and weak standards affect many projects.
context_reasoning: Needs deep knowledge of the organisation's products, risks, history and people, built over months.

domain_reasoning: Writing the diagnosis and recommendations is a document-writing task.
length_reasoning: A short write-up of a simple problem takes under half an hour; a complex diagnosis with evidence takes a couple of hours.
review_reasoning: The reviewer reads the write-up and checks the diagnosis against the evidence; deeper checking needs the original logs.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong diagnosis sent to a customer or developers wastes effort and can be reversed, but a wrong recommendation to a customer causes rework.
context_reasoning: Needs the product and customer environment details, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Most of the time goes into running the product and the defect tracker to retest the fix and update the ticket.
length_reasoning: A quick retest of a simple fix takes a few minutes; a fix needing a complex setup or several regression checks takes an hour.
review_reasoning: The reviewer reads the note and repeats the test steps on the build, which is quick for simple defects.
stakes_reasoning: A missed bad fix is usually found later by the team, but can reach customers if the defect is serious.
context_reasoning: Needs the product's behaviour and the team's workflow, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Most of the time goes into working in the defect tracker or database: searching, merging and editing records.
length_reasoning: A small pass on a tidy database takes half an hour; a big pass before a release with many duplicates takes a few hours.
review_reasoning: The lead checks a sample of merges and updated statuses and the known-issues list against the database.
stakes_reasoning: Wrongly merged or stale records mislead support and developers, but they can be restored and noticed soon.
context_reasoning: Needs deep knowledge of the product's defect history and what counts as a duplicate, built over months.

domain_reasoning: Reading the question and writing the reply is a text task, with some looking up of documentation.
length_reasoning: A common question takes a few minutes to answer; an unusual one needing research or reproduction takes most of an hour.
review_reasoning: The lead reads the question and reply and checks the advice is correct and clear.
stakes_reasoning: Wrong instructions to a user cause rework or a repeat ticket but can be corrected.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's systems and software and users' setup, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Most of the time goes into using diagnostic tools, remote access and system settings on the user's machine.
length_reasoning: A simple fix takes a quarter of an hour; a hard problem needing manuals and repeated follow-up takes hours of active work.
review_reasoning: The lead reads the ticket notes and checks the fix and outcome; deeper checks need a look at the user's system.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong fix annoys the user and costs time, and a bad change can lose data or cause an outage.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's machines, software standards and network, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Scoping, writing scripts and briefing participants is mostly writing and email, with some tool set-up.
length_reasoning: A small round with a few participants takes a couple of hours; a large third-party round with many scripts and access takes days.
review_reasoning: The manager reads the plan, scripts and schedule and checks scope and access, which takes a while for a full round.
stakes_reasoning: A poorly planned round wastes participants' time and delays testing, but can be redone.
context_reasoning: Needs the product, test goals and who the participants are, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Most of the time goes into operating testing tools and the test management tool.
length_reasoning: A short automated or smoke run takes about ten minutes of active work; a long manual run with many cases takes hours.
review_reasoning: The lead checks the logged results against the run and spot-checks failures and evidence.
stakes_reasoning: Wrongly recorded results are usually caught but a missed failure can lead to a bad release decision.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's tools, environments and test conventions, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Most of the time goes into entering case details and routing the referral in the case or ticketing system.
length_reasoning: A simple referral takes a few minutes; one needing the history gathered and summarised takes about twenty.
review_reasoning: The receiving department reads the referral and checks the case details are complete.
stakes_reasoning: Missing details delay the grievance a little and are caught by the receiving department.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's departments, routing rules and case system, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Keeping the log is writing short entries through the day and filing it; the work is mostly text.
length_reasoning: Active time is the sum of short entries and filing, from a quiet day to a busy installation day.
review_reasoning: The supervisor reads the day's entries and checks they are complete; an auditor may compare some to other records.
stakes_reasoning: A missing entry is mostly an internal gap but can matter in an audit.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's systems and logging conventions, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into reading the policy terms and writing the note.
length_reasoning: A clear-cut coverage question takes a few minutes; one needing detailed policy reading or exclusions takes about twenty.
review_reasoning: A reviewer listens to the call and checks the answer against the policy and the note.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong coverage answer sets the customer's expectations and can cause complaints or regulatory exposure.
context_reasoning: Needs the insurer's policy forms and coverage rules, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Evaluating and recommending is mostly reading, testing and writing a report.
length_reasoning: A small software evaluation takes a couple of hours; a hardware or upgrade evaluation with testing and costing takes days.
review_reasoning: The manager reads the report and checks the reasoning and costs, which takes a while for a big decision.
stakes_reasoning: A bad recommendation can lead to wasted spend or a poor purchase that is hard to undo.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the employer's systems, needs and budget, learned over weeks to months.
